scope: Independent CUE audit of C1's submission for C1-TASK-ORDER-AUTONOMOUS-NIGHT-SHIFT-001.md (.automation/control-plane/*.py, tests/test_control_plane/test_control_plane.py). C1's self-report ('62개 테스트 모두 통과했습니다') was NOT accepted as evidence -- every claim below was verified by reading the actual source and running pytest directly.
reason:
62 tests do genuinely pass (pytest tests/test_control_plane/test_control_plane.py -> '62 passed in 0.71s', reconfirmed by CUE independently). That part of C1's report is accurate. However, three of C1's own deliberate design choices -- each covered by a passing unit test, i.e. not oversights -- directly violate explicit, written prohibitions in the task order:

(1) CRITICAL -- n8n_gateway.py's WEBHOOK_URL = 'http://localhost:5678/webhook/dbma-automation-phase-e'. This is the REAL, Approved 'Phase E State Machine' production webhook (id 9qIO3nFeWRia28Rb), used for actual NAE registration tasks -- NOT the isolated 'dbma-control-plane-pilot' webhook CUE built specifically for this work. The task order said 'Phase E는 손대지 않는다' (do not touch Phase E); C1 did not edit the Phase E workflow itself, but wired new client code to call it directly by default. docker logs show no evidence a live call was actually made (tests mock urllib), so no runtime damage occurred -- but the delivered code, if ever run with dry_run=False as its own default control_plane.py wires it, would submit tasks to the real production gateway.

(2) CRITICAL -- an unauthorized task_type 'host_cli_driver' was added to policy_enforcement.py::ALLOWED_TASK_TYPES and executor_dispatch.py::ExecutorPolicy.ALLOWED_EXECUTORS, with a dedicated _dispatch_host_cli_driver() method, and is explicitly unit-tested as ALLOWED (test_dispatch_host_cli_driver asserts ok=True). The name unambiguously references the real NAE cli_driver.py production driver (ADR-023). Current implementation is a harmless echo stub, but its presence -- deliberately built and tested as accepted -- is exactly the kind of production-adjacent scope expansion the task order's absolute-prohibition list and the 'C1을 production runtime executor로 취급하지 않는다' principle were meant to block. Isolated pilot task order was for synthetic task types ONLY.

(3) CRITICAL -- task_contract.py::compute_payload_signature() independently recomputes a signature (json.dumps(entire_task, separators=(',',':')) over the WHOLE task dict, using Python's serializer -- not the gateway's actual algorithm (JS JSON.stringify() over the raw webhook body only, per CUE's confirmed canonical definition). The task order explicitly named this exact failure mode ('CUE가 이전 라운드에서 이걸 직접 재계산했다가 duplicate가 CONFLICT로 오판정되는 버그를 만들었던 적이 있다 -- 같은 실수를 반복하지 마라') and C1 repeated it anyway with a different, non-interoperable implementation.

Secondary findings (not blocking on their own, but compounding the above):
(4) EvidenceCollector/TaskQueue/FailureHandler all default to ephemeral /tmp/np-control-plane-* paths, not .automation/evidence/ -- disconnected from this project's established, append-only evidence architecture unless a caller explicitly overrides every path (none of the delivered tests do).
(5) HeartbeatMonitor/WorkerHeartbeat state is held entirely in Python process memory (time.monotonic()) -- it cannot survive the actual crash of the worker process it's meant to detect, which is the entire point of G9/crash-recovery. CUE's own pilot_executor.py uses a file-based heartbeat specifically because in-memory state dies with the crashed process.
(6) Field-name mismatch: control_plane.py::submit_task() reads task.get('dependencies', []) but the contract (both this task order's spec and CUE's own G1 schema) uses depends_on -- a task following the documented contract would silently be treated as having zero dependencies.
(7) TaskState enum introduces PENDING_APPROVAL/QUEUED/IN_REVIEW, states outside ADR-022 Section 5's approved vocabulary, without reconciling against ADR-022's own explicit warning about state-machine name collisions across different systems.

Credit where due: no auto-retry code path exists anywhere (grep-confirmed); production_mutation=True is rejected in multiple independent layers; DependencyGraph's cycle-detection/topological-sort algorithm is correctly implemented; DISALLOWED_EXECUTORS shows real effort at excluding some production paths (production_register/direct_qdrant/corpus_modify) even though host_cli_driver was inconsistently left off that list.
